channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: FAA ends ground stop after thousands of aircraft around the country were halted for more than four hours
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration said the cause of the disruption was a “temporary telecommunications outage.” An FAA spokesperson confirmed that the ground stop had been lifted.

item.title: Trump to meet with Putin and Xi at summit in China next week, White House says, their first trilateral meeting
item.description: The high-stakes gathering of three geopolitical superpowers in Shenzhen comes as the American president reels from election losses at home and an espionage scandal threatens to deepen tensions with China. An administration official said no separate bilateral meeting between Trump and Putin was planned.

item.title: Behind Jensen Huang’s spy scandal, a shadow war for Trump’s ear on China
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s intervention helped topple one of Washington’s most influential corporate voices on China, giving momentum to officials pushing for tougher restrictions.

item.title: I served in the Old Guard. Pete Hegseth was treated without fear or favor.
item.description: "The Old Guard offers powerful antidotes: high standards, humility to accept correction and the confidence to hold others to account," Mikhael Smits writes.

item.title: Judge clashes again with Justice Department lawyers as she weighs D.C. golf course’s future days before scheduled closure
item.description: After another heated hearing, U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes is expected to rule Saturday on whether East Potomac Golf Links can close. President Donald Trump wants to turn the land into a championship course.

item.title: FAA grounds flights at all U.S. airports, citing communications issue
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the nationwide ground stop was due to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.”

item.title: Supreme Court to review legality of Trump policy blocking asylum seekers at border, a key piece of his immigration agenda
item.description: The case is one of several high-profile immigration matters the Supreme Court has agreed to review in the coming months.

item.title: Rep. Lauren Boebert (R) loses reelection to retired Navy Rear Adm. Eileen Laubacher (D), according to AP
item.description: Boebert, who came to epitomize the most aggressive politics of the MAGA era, was seen as a lock to keep her Colorado seat just a year ago.

item.title: Joe Biden defends his 2024 run and reckons with Trump in new memoir
item.description: In “Promise Me, America,” Biden revisits the pandemic and the effort to rally allies behind Ukraine, while defending his decision to seek a second term. The Washington Post obtained a copy of the memoir in advance of its public release Tuesday.

item.title: Catahoula is not the same old take on New Orleans cuisine, writes dining critic Elazar Sontag
item.description: The Navy Yard restaurant, which opened earlier this year, reflects the many layers of Louisiana cuisine.

item.title: I don’t want to go home for Christmas. Should I tell my family why? Carolyn Hax is giving advice.
item.description: Our advice columnist is answering your questions about the strange train we call life.

item.title: At the Tomb of the Unknowns, Pete Hegseth could not hear the silence that others hold sacred, columnist Philip Kennicott writes
item.description: The defense secretary and his group laughed, joked and bantered as if they were at a garden party during a visit to the Tomb at Arlington National Cemetery. An ordinary soldier, on behalf of those who have died for their country, demanded respect from the man who styles himself the secretary of war, our columnist writes.

item.title: The anti-Democratic Party won — and shows the way forward
item.description: The midterms rewarded mavericks who criticized their own side and responded to local communities.

item.title: A fifth person was injured in a D.C. shooting that killed one man, police say. See how the deadly attack unfolded in Logan Circle.
item.description: Police announced Friday that there was a sixth victim, an adult female with a nonfatal injury. View the visual forensics investigation from The Post that details how the gunman attacked people at a gym and condominium in Northwest Washington on Thursday.

item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blames Commerce for not cracking down on company that was a Nvidia customer
item.description: Singapore’s Megaspeed is at the heart of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s spy-sex scandal. The Commerce Department had been investigating if Megaspeed breached U.S. export restrictions on computer chips.

item.title: Microsoft says services are improving in North America and Europe, even as international outages continue into second day
item.description: The technology giant said that some users appeared to regain access to services such as Outlook and Teams in North America and much of Europe. Governments and businesses in Asia also reported being affected by the outage.

item.title: D.C. shooting. Vance’s 2028 plans. Chris Van Hollen. Pete Hegseth. Building collapse. Inflation. Healthy chocolate. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Sen. Chris Van Hollen challenges Sen. Chuck Schumer to lead Democratic majority in next Congress
item.description: Schumer (New York) has led Senate Democrats for the past decade and never before faced a challenger. If Van Hollen (Maryland) is successful in his uphill bid, he would preside over a majority of at least 55 members that could stymie President Donald Trump’s agenda during his final two years in the White House. “The voters called for big change, and this is a time that we have to deliver for people across the country,” Van Hollen said about his decision.

item.title: Welcome to ‘The Vow,’ the dating show for budding tradwives. It’s really something, columnist Monica Hesse writes.
item.description: Earlier this year, the nation was experiencing what appeared to be a deeply felt interest in returning us to the (18)50s. And then the midterms happened. So “The Vow” — Fox Nation’s new dating reality show for people seeking “traditional” marriage — has arrived at an odd time.

item.title: Just after he shot five people, D.C. gunman said he had ‘to do something’ to draw attention to his condo dispute
item.description: Matt Lambert told a building manager after he shot five people in Washington, D.C., that he was tired of the mold and water damage in his unit. In 2025, Lambert filed a lawsuit against the condo association and property management company.

item.title: Police identify deceased victim in Logan Circle shooting as a manager at the condo building where the gunman lived
item.description: Authorities said James Stuart, 46, was shot with a handgun at a Vida Fitness gym near 15th and P streets NW.

item.title: Conservatives are warning Vance to skip 2028. That might not be necessary.
item.description: Conservatives are warning Vance to skip 2028. That might not be necessary.

item.title: U.S. says Europeans will join talks on ending Ukraine war, overcoming Putin’s objections
item.description: Russia has resisted a European role in the negotiations, and President Vladimir Putin on Thursday reiterated his opposition to European peacekeepers.

item.title: Man who shot 5 in D.C. was a doctor who lived nearby, officials said, and had long-running dispute with condo building’s management
item.description: The attacker who opened fire in the Logan Circle neighborhood Thursday morning, killing one person and wounding four others, has been identified as Matt Lambert, a 55-year-old doctor, according to two officials. Records show that Lambert had filed a lawsuit alleging that his building’s condo association failed to act on his complaints about a mold problem and water damage inside his unit.

item.title: Hegseth awards a medal to soldier who admonished him and his team for talking loudly, laughing at Tomb of the Unknowns
item.description: A video of the incident, which followed a Veterans Day observance, elicited furious backlash from critics incredulous that a defense secretary would behave disrespectfully at one of the nation’s most sacred memorials.

item.title: Trump says no deal needed with Iran, closes down Vance negotiations
item.description: Vice President JD Vance in recent days had started outreach to hard-liners in Tehran to explore the possibility of a negotiated end to the conflict. The war — and the jump in gas and food prices that has come with it — is deeply unpopular among U.S. voters, who delivered a historic defeat to Republicans in the midterm elections last week.

item.title: Witnesses describe early moments of shooting on Logan Circle corner
item.description: Some fled a Vida gym after gunfire erupted, barricading themselves in a basement. Others tried to help a bleeding woman crumpled on the curb. One person was killed and four were injured in the shooting Thursday morning; police said the attacker was dead of an apparently self-inflicted gunshot wound after barricading themselves in an apartment.

item.title: 1 person killed, 4 injured in shooting that began in D.C. gym; suspect shot himself, police say
item.description: Interim D.C. police chief Jeffery Carroll said the gunman opened fire at a Vida Fitness gym near the intersection of 15th and P streets NW. The suspected attacker later barricaded himself inside a nearby apartment building, Carroll said, then shot himself after speaking to police for more than an hour.

item.title: Trump’s golden Oval Office defies the president who created it
item.description: William Howard Taft avoided foreign wars and worked to reduce tariffs. His presidency was “humdrum.”

item.title: At least 5 injured in Logan Circle shooting; police issue shelter-in-place warning during barricade situation
item.description: Police were “working an active barricade” near the shooting, which occurred near the intersection of 15th and P streets NW, according to a department spokesperson.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after affair with alleged spy
item.description: Huang resigned amid reports of two affairs that included a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, a stunning downfall for one of the world’s most powerful executives.

item.title: Multiple victims in shooting in D.C.’s Logan Circle
item.description: D.C. police were searching for a suspect Thursday morning. A police spokesperson said the shooting happened at the intersection of 15th and P streets Northwest.

item.title: At least eight dead and at least 17 injured after Brooklyn building collapse
item.description: Among those injured in the three-story building collapse in Brooklyn on Wednesday were three firefighters, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday.

item.title: Mississippi result. Trump probes. Hegseth scolded. Nvidia CEO. El Niño. Housing market. Mysterious meowing. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: He learned he has 35 siblings. Here’s how he aired his family secret.
item.description: Noam Tomaschoff found out that the man who raised him was not his biological father. He dealt with it the best way he knew how.

item.title: Nvidia board will meet to weigh fate of CEO Jensen Huang after his affair with alleged spy
item.description: Nvidia’s board is expected to meet late Wednesday, according to two people familiar with the matter, days after Huang admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia stock fell in after-hours trading following news reports of the board’s meeting and a second alleged affair by Huang with an Nvidia executive who reported to him.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom narrowly ousts Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) in deep-red Mississippi, AP reports
item.description: Mississippi last sent a Democrat to the Senate in 1982, and no African American had won statewide since Reconstruction.

item.title: Hegseth and his entourage scolded by military sentinel at Tomb of the Unknowns
item.description: The defense secretary, his wife and aides were admonished after they were observed laughing and talking during a visit to the sacred site at Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: What a child’s compliment tells me about Pete Hegseth
item.description: What a child’s compliment tells me about Pete Hegseth

item.title: How Trump maneuvered to the brink of building his 250-foot triumphal arch
item.description: The president’s proposal for the massive monument won final approval from review panels, but it faces a lawsuit that may head to the Supreme Court.

item.title: See where El Niño may help deliver lots of snow this winter
item.description: Some places could end up with far more snow than they bargained for.

item.title: Why do restaurants close before their posted hours? Our food critic is taking questions.
item.description: Washington Post food critic Elazar Sontag entertains your restaurant questions, rants and raves.

item.title: What one town’s 300 percent rise in home prices says about New England
item.description: The region needs affordable starter homes. They’re basically banned.

item.title: White House readies aggressive fight against planned investigations by Congress
item.description: The counsel’s office is beefing up staffing and warning Democrats against “capricious threats,” but private firms may be wary of aiding the pushback.

item.title: Veterans tried ayahuasca to ease their PTSD. It changed them, they said.
item.description: The Coming Home Project, which works to end veteran suicide, hosted a group of veterans at a medically licensed psychedelics retreat in Costa Rica.

item.title: Flying by pricey military jet, Marco Rubio rarely misses a football game at University of Florida, where his son plays
item.description: The secretary of state, who is required to travel by government plane, defended his trips to his alma mater.

item.title: Pete Hegseth. Minority leader. Trump’s arch. Rubio flights. Winter snow. Thriving workers. Air purifiers. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Kennedy family sues to stop Trump’s triumphal arch, saying it will cast a shadow on John F. Kennedy’s gravesite
item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have sued the Trump administration to block the planned 250-foot-tall structure, which they said would “damage historically significant sightlines to the existing gravesites and memorials” at Arlington National Cemetery. A Post analysis found that the arch would briefly cover Kennedy’s memorial on 50 days of the year and his eternal flame on 18 days, while touching burial sites across the cemetery on 284 days over the year.

item.title: Hegseth escapes impeachment threat as House Republicans unite to prevent a vote
item.description: The result follows a coordinated effort within the Trump administration, including by the president, to defend the defense secretary. Hegseth held a rare Pentagon news conference Tuesday, during which he appealed directly to the president and his allies in Congress. The attempt to remove him from office had been led by Rep. Thomas Massie, a fellow Republican and frequent critic of President Donald Trump.

item.title: Supreme Court grapples with arguments over the power of federal agencies to impose fines
item.description: The case comes as the high court’s conservative majority has pared back the power of federal regulators in a series of recent cases. But even some conservatives appeared skeptical on Tuesday of going further.
